subject.title: feat(goal-driver): completion contracts, wait barriers, and an optional completion judge

question: After the deterministic defects are fixed, should OpenClaw intentionally add these non-Codex goal APIs, and should the provider-backed completion judge be reviewed separately?
rationale: Direct Codex inspection shows these additions are optional OpenClaw policy, provider-cost, and durable-state surfaces rather than required runtime parity.

options.title: Stage deterministic first
options.body: Land completion contracts and explicit barriers after the base, then evaluate the LLM judge in a separate proposal.

options.title: Sponsor the combined experiment
options.body: Keep all three together only with explicit ownership, repaired lifecycle behavior, and feature-specific live proof.

options.title: Stay deterministic
options.body: Decline the new core APIs and keep the goal driver aligned with Codex's deterministic contract.

recommendation.title: Stage deterministic first
recommendation.body: Land completion contracts and explicit barriers after the base, then evaluate the LLM judge in a separate proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-main history signal for the session-path and simple-completion seams affected by this product choice.
